payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Alysa, Chong, Junie, Shantel

payload.content: Hello team, I am Junie. I have strong skills in data-science and infrastructure, and 8 hours available. I am considering the medium-priority infrastructure tasks (implement, review, test) since they match my skills and availability. Please share your preferences so we can avoid overlaps and optimize task coverage.

To all, I note the low-priority frontend tasks are less aligned with my skills and have high costs, so I prefer not to claim those. I am prioritizing the medium-priority infrastructure tasks given my skills and availability. Please share your plans so we can coordinate effectively.

Hello team, I am Shantel. My top skills are infrastructure and mobile-development, and I have 8 hours available. I see Junie is focusing on medium-priority infrastructure tasks, which is a good match for their skills. I am considering taking on the low-priority mobile-development frontend tasks since they align well with my skills and availability and to avoid overlap with Junie's plan.

To coordinate better, I suggest Junie takes the medium-priority infrastructure tasks while I cover the low-priority frontend tasks. This way we maximize task coverage without duplication and align with our strengths.

Hello team, I am Chong. My top skill is infrastructure with 10 hours available. I see Junie is interested in medium-priority infrastructure tasks and Shantel plans to cover low-priority frontend tasks. I am also interested in medium-priority infrastructure tasks, especially those that fit my availability and skills well. Let's coordinate to avoid overlaps and cover as many tasks as possible.

Hello team, this is Alysa. I have top skills in infrastructure and data-science, and 10 hours available. I see Junie and Chong are interested in medium-priority infrastructure tasks, and Shantel is focusing on low-priority frontend tasks. To maximize coverage and avoid overlap, I suggest Junie and Chong split the medium-priority infrastructure tasks, and Shantel covers the frontend tasks as planned. I am considering the medium-priority infrastructure review or test tasks if they remain unclaimed, given my skills and availability.

Greetings team, Alysa here. I note Junie, Chong, and Shantel's task preferences. I will hold off claiming tasks until I see your final intentions to avoid duplication and optimize our collective task coverage. Please share your final choices soon so we can finalize assignments efficiently.

To all, I propose I take the ISSUE-0002::implement task, Chong and Alysa split the ISSUE-0002::review and ISSUE-0002::test tasks, and Shantel covers the low-priority frontend tasks. This division maximizes coverage and fits our skills and availability well. Please share your feedback.

Hello team, Shantel here. I agree with Junie's proposal for me to cover the low-priority frontend tasks given my skills and availability. I plan to focus on the ISSUE-0001::triage task which fits well within my 8-hour limit and aligns with my mobile-development skill. This will complement Junie's, Chong's, and Alysa's focus on medium-priority infrastructure tasks and help maximize total task coverage without overlap.

I encourage Alysa, Chong, and Junie to finalize their task choices soon so we can efficiently assign tasks and avoid duplication. I will wait for your final preferences before committing my choice in the next phase.

Hello team, I agree with the proposed division: Junie takes ISSUE-0002::implement, I will take ISSUE-0002::review, Alysa can take ISSUE-0002::test, and Shantel covers the low-priority frontend tasks. This plan maximizes task coverage and aligns well with our skills and availability. Please confirm your final choices soon.

Hello team, Alysa here. I agree with the proposed division: Junie takes ISSUE-0002::implement, Chong takes ISSUE-0002::review, I will take ISSUE-0002::test, and Shantel covers low-priority frontend tasks like ISSUE-0001::triage. This plan optimizes task coverage, matches skills, and fits our availability well. Looking forward to final confirmations to proceed with assignments.

Reiterating to all, I will hold the ISSUE-0002::test task if no conflicts arise, as it aligns with my skills and availability, to maximize medium-priority task completion. Please confirm your final task choices soon.
